raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Lets vLLM load ModelOpt checkpoints whose routed-expert NVFP4 block scales are CSF-compressed. Each layer names its format in `quantized_layers[...]["weight_scale_encoding"]`, and two formats ship today: `csf` in `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local` and `csf_32x2_v1` in `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local`. This started from #60646 (draft since Oct 8); its two commits are still in the history, and the `csf` decoder comes from it.

## Claims

- `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` takes the CSF streams as its own params, decodes each scale matrix once all of its streams have arrived, and loads it through the scale param's own weight loader. TP and EP sharding, the MoE backends and the kernels see the same E4M3 scales as with an uncompressed checkpoint.
- Each encoding is one entry in `layers/quantization/utils/csf_scales.py`: its stream names and its decoder. The ModelOpt config renames `<proj>.weight_scale.<stream>` to the method's params, so model loaders don't change.
- A stream param sets `weight_loader_target` to the scale it fills. `track_weights_loading` counts the scale as loaded through it, and layerwise reload leaves its loader unwrapped so the scale's own wrapper buffers and counts the load.
- Both decoders are lossless against NVIDIA's reference decoders.
- An unknown encoding, or an encoding on a non-NVFP4 layer, fails when the config is built. An encoding on any layer other than routed experts, including one shard of a fused linear, fails in `get_quant_method`. Malformed streams and matrices with missing streams raise instead of loading wrong bytes.

## Validation

On CPU, main (`dc45a5f552`) plus this PR:

```text
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_csf_scales.py  # 13 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py    # 9 passed
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py      # 64 passed, 33 skipped, 1 failed, 2 errors
pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py                   # 109 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed, 3 errors
pre-commit run --files <changed files>                       # passed
```

The failures and errors in `test_reload.py` and `test_modelopt.py` start an engine and need a GPU, which was hidden for this run; they fail the same way without this PR. The new `test_registry.py` and `test_reload.py` cases and the stream test in `test_csf_scales.py` fail without the `weight_loader_target` handling.

`csf`: all 73,728 scale matrices in a local copy of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local decode byte-identical to `decode_csf_slab_scales` in NVIDIA's reference implementation, with up to 13,793 exceptions in one matrix and no stream pair split across shards. The whole decode takes 25.3 s in one process.

`csf_32x2_v1`: 378 GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local matrices fetched from the Hub (every CSF layer, three experts each, gate/up/down) decode byte-identical to `decode_csf_scales` in the same reference.

End to end on two SM80 GPUs with TP=2, running this PR's Python against the compiled ops of nightly `0.32.1rc1.dev467+g444d69110`: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local (`--language-model-only`) loads with `enable_weights_track` and no missing weights, holds 96 decoded scale params per rank, and answers five greedy prompts correctly. `reload_weights` then processes all 48 CSF MoE layers on each rank with no delayed or failed loads, and leaves the scale checksums and the greedy outputs unchanged.

## Details

The decode happens at load time rather than in `process_weights_after_loading` because the compressed streams can't be TP-sliced: holding them until then would keep every layer's compressed scales on each rank. The streams add up to 4.0 GB in Qwen3.8 and 10.3 GB in GLM-5.3, summed from the safetensors headers. The stream params are empty, so they never reach kernels or EPLB.

The decoders run in numpy rather than torch: every small torch op goes through the intra-op thread pool, which the loader sizes to CPUs per local worker, and that made the `csf` decode about 1.7x slower in #60646's form.

Both checkpoints keep weights in a `tensors/` subdirectory, which the default loader doesn't search yet: all 21 Qwen3.8 shards, and the 214 attention and indexer tensors of GLM-5.3. Neither loads in full from the Hub until that lookup lands in #64739.

Not a duplicate: #63908 decodes CSF inside the Qwen4Exp NVIDIA model file. Searching open PRs for "CSF", "weight_scale_encoding" and "nvfp4_csf" turns up nothing else.

Like #60646, this doesn't keep the scales compressed in GPU memory; that needs kernels that read compressed scales.

Done in c22209f980. `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` now registers the CSF streams named by the layer's `weight_scale_encoding` as its own params, and the ModelOpt config renames `weight_scale.<stream>` to match them. The decoders sit in `layers/quantization/utils/csf_scales.py`, keyed by encoding, with `csf_32x2_v1` next to `csf`. The default loader no longer decodes CSF.

One change from what I wrote above: the method decodes each scale matrix as soon as all of its streams have arrived, not in `process_weights_after_loading`. The streams can't be TP-sliced, so holding them until then would keep every layer's compressed scales on each rank: 4.0 GB for Qwen3.8 and 10.3 GB for GLM-5.3, summed from the checkpoint headers. The decoded matrix goes through the scale param's own weight loader, so TP and EP sharding work as they do for an uncompressed checkpoint.

A stream param fills a different param, so I mark it with `weight_loader_target`. `track_weights_loading` uses it to count the scale as loaded, and layerwise reload leaves those loaders unwrapped so the scale's wrapper buffers and counts the load. Without it, `enable_weights_track` reported the scales as missing, and reload held every CSF layer until finalize.

I also took the `tensors/` shard lookup out of this PR and will send it separately. Until then, neither checkpoint loads in full from the Hub: Qwen3.8 keeps all of its shards under `tensors/`, and GLM-5.3 keeps its attention weights there.

Checked end to end on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local with TP=2: it loads and generates correctly, and `reload_weights` processes every CSF layer and keeps the outputs unchanged. Details are in the description.

Thanks for the review, and for starting this in #60646.

1. The `tensors/` lookup is up in #64739. It also covers GLM-5.3, which keeps one shard under `tensors/` next to the root shards.
2. Agreed, only one should land. This one handles both `csf` and `csf_32x2_v1` in the quant method, so the model file doesn't need its own decoder.

Independent-implementation datapoint, in case it helps: I had a model-local CSF decoder for this exact checkpoint in #63908 (now closed as superseded by this PR). A few notes from validating it against `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local`:

- The checkpoint carries **147,456 CSF stream tensors** — all on routed experts (`mlp.experts.*` `gate/up/down_proj.weight_scale.nvfp4_csf_{fixed,exceptions}`); the `linear_attn.*` NVFP4 scales are already plain `weight_scale`. So the routed-experts-only scope here matches what the checkpoint actually needs today.
- My decoder (`base + nibble codes`, low nibble first, 24-bit position / 8-bit value exception scatter) is byte-identical in algorithm to `_decode_csf`; I diffed decoded scale bytes against the uncompressed reference on real layers and got an exact match.
- Two edge cases worth having in the tests (both covered by my 3 unit tests, happy to port): `exceptions.numel() == 0` (checkpoints with no fixups), and the `float8_e4m3fn` reinterp view must be taken on the **uint8** decoded buffer (a cast would silently reinterpret rather than re-view — the bug my PR title was about).

Also 👍 the numpy-vs-torch choice for the decode itself — at ~74K scale pairs the per-op thread-pool sync dominates; I saw that too when the torch-op version ran multi-threaded loading.

All inline threads are resolved or outdated after the move to the quantization side. @stecasta @Isotr0py could you take a fresh look at the current diff and confirm the new `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` registration addresses the placement concern from #60646? Once it's approved we can go through the `ready` label / CI path.

I don't think this is a correct method to deal with this. We should implement csf scale support at quantization side instead.

The checkpoint already declares `weight_scale_encoding` per layer, so ModelOpt should pick and validate it instead of the default loader guessing from tensor suffixes.

I'm considering moving the decoder under `layers/quantization/utils/` and adding a small quant-config hook in `AutoWeightsLoader` to decode the stream pairs before TP slicing. The existing checkpoint mapper only handles names, so this would be a new hook. Would that fit the direction you had in mind?

I'd keep the subdirectory shard lookup in a separate change.

I think the root cause is that we can't deal with this scale format natively and have to convert it back to E4M3 as workaround before weights loading. I don't see we have corresponding quant method implented for it, so maybe we should implement the quant method for it.
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa3b9d1377219247060d3c8b49eae199c9e7e154/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L2517-L2529

NVIDIA uses CSF on more than one checkpoint. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local uses `csf`, and GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local uses `csf_32x2_v1`, which lays out the streams differently. Both only put it on the routed experts.

So instead of the loader hook I mentioned above, I'd follow the `FormatScheme` pattern in `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`. From each layer's `weight_scale_encoding`, the method would register the CSF streams as its own params and load them as they are, and `process_weights_after_loading` would decode them into `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale`. The ModelOpt config would rename the stream suffixes to match those params. The decoders would live under `layers/quantization/utils/`, keyed by encoding, so `csf_32x2_v1` gets its own params and decoder in the same place.

I haven't written this yet. So far I've loaded and served the checkpoint with this PR's decoder through a plugin, with TP=2 (nightly, MTP on) and with PP=2.

I'll add `csf_32x2_v1` in this PR as well, and split it out if you'd rather review it separately.

Hi @lesj0610, thanks for taking this over from #60646 and moving it to the quantization side. Two points inline, plus:

1. Neither checkpoint loads from the Hub until the `tensors/` lookup lands. Could you link that PR here once it's up, so the two can be reviewed together?
2. #63908 decodes `csf` inside the Qwen4Exp model file. With both merged, Qwen3.8 would take whichever path sees the stream names first, so I think only one should land, and this one covers both encodings.

This supersedes my draft #60646, so I'll close that one.

IIUC this accepts an encoding on any NVFP4 layer, but only `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` registers the stream params. On a linear layer the renamed `weight_scale_<stream>` names would have no param to land in, so the load either fails on an unknown name or, in a model loop that skips unknown names, leaves `weight_scale` unloaded with no error (weight tracking is off by default for quantized models). Both checkpoints only encode routed experts today, so could `get_quant_method` reject an encoding on anything that isn't `RoutedExperts`?

+# - ``csf``: ``nvfp4_csf_fixed`` (uint8, ``[rows // 16, 16 * (1 + cols // 2)]``)
+#   holds, per 16-row slab, one base byte per row followed by the rows' 4-bit
+#   codes, two per byte, low nibble first; a scale byte is ``base + code``.
+#   ``nvfp4_csf_exceptions`` (uint32) holds sorted words whose low 24 bits are
+#   a flat ``row * cols + col`` position and whose high 8 bits replace that
+#   byte.
+# - ``csf_32x2_v1``: ``csf32_bases`` (uint8, one per row) and ``csf32_codes``
+#   (uint8, 4-bit codes) cover 32-row x 2-column blocks, grouped into 128 x 4
+#   tiles, 32 tiles to a page. ``csf32_exceptions`` (uint16) holds the in-block
+#   position in the low byte and the scale byte in the high byte;
+#   ``csf32_page_bases`` (uint32, byte offset of each page's first exception)
+#   and ``csf32_offsets`` (uint16, per page a 0 then each block's exception
+#   end) index them.
+
+# numpy keeps these small ops off torch's intra-op thread pool, whose per-op
+# sync dominates when weight loading runs with many threads.
+
+
+def _decode_csf(fixed: torch.Tensor, exceptions: torch.Tensor) -> np.ndarray:
+    if fixed.dtype != torch.uint8 or fixed.dim() != 2 or fixed.shape[1] % 16:
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid CSF fixed stream {fixed.dtype} {fixed.shape}")
+    if exceptions.dtype != torch.uint32:
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid CSF exceptions dtype {exceptions.dtype}")
+    rows = fixed.shape[0] * 16
+    cols = (fixed.shape[1] // 16 - 1) * 2
+    if rows * cols > 1 << 24:
+        raise ValueError("CSF scale exceeds 24-bit exception positions")
+    raw = fixed.numpy()
+    bases = raw[:, :16].reshape(rows, 1)
+    if (bases > 240).any():
+        raise ValueError("CSF row bases must be in 0..240")
+    packed = raw[:, 16:].reshape(rows, cols // 2)
+    codes = np.stack((packed & 0xF, packed >> 4), axis=-1).reshape(rows, cols)
+    out = (bases + codes).reshape(-1)
+    words = exceptions.reshape(-1).numpy()
+    positions = words & 0xFFFFFF
+    if positions.size and (
+        positions[-1] >= rows * cols or (positions[1:] <= positions[:-1]).any()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("CSF exception positions must be increasing and in range")
+    out[positions] = words >> 24
+    return out.reshape(rows, cols)
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _csf32_blocks(rows: int, cols: int):
+    """Origin, width and page of each 32x2 block in storage order, and the flat
+    ``[rows, cols]`` position of each code."""
+    tile_r, tile_c, pair, block = np.meshgrid(
+        np.arange(-(-rows // 128)),
+        np.arange(-(-cols // 4)),
+        np.arange(2),
+        np.arange(4),
+        indexing="ij",
+    )
+    r0 = (128 * tile_r + 32 * block).ravel()
+    c0 = (4 * tile_c + 2 * pair).ravel()
+    page = (tile_r * tile_c.shape[1] + tile_c).ravel() // 32
+    keep = (r0 < rows) & (c0 < cols)
+    r0, c0, page = r0[keep], c0[keep], page[keep]
+    width = np.minimum(cols - c0, 2)
+    i, j = np.meshgrid(np.arange(32), np.arange(2), indexing="ij")
+    cells = (r0[:, None, None] + i) * cols + c0[:, None, None] + j
+    return r0, c0, width, page, cells[j < width[:, None, None]]
+
+
+def _decode_csf_32x2(
+    bases: torch.Tensor,
+    codes: torch.Tensor,
+    page_bases: torch.Tensor,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor,
+    exceptions: torch.Tensor,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    dtypes = (torch.uint8, torch.uint8, torch.uint32, torch.uint16, torch.uint16)
+    streams = (bases, codes, page_bases, offsets, exceptions)
+    rows = bases.numel()
+    cols = 2 * codes.numel() // max(rows, 1)
+    if (
+        any(t.dtype != d for t, d in zip(streams, dtypes))
+        or rows % 32
+        or rows * cols != 2 * codes.numel()
+        or cols == 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid csf_32x2_v1 streams")
+    r0, c0, width, page, cells = _csf32_blocks(rows, cols)
+    num_pages = int(page[-1]) + 1
+    base, packed, origins, index, words = (t.reshape(-1).numpy() for t in streams)
+    if origins.size != num_pages or index.size != r0.size + num_pages:
+        raise ValueError("Invalid csf_32x2_v1 index sizes")
+    if (base > 240).any():
+        raise ValueError("CSF row bases must be in 0..240")
+    out = np.empty(rows * cols, dtype=np.uint8)
+    out[cells] = np.stack((packed & 0xF, packed >> 4), -1).ravel() + base[cells // cols]
+
+    first = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(page, prepend=-1))
+    ends = origins[page].astype(np.int64) // 2 + index[np.arange(r0.size) + page + 1]
+    starts = np.concatenate(([0], ends[:-1]))
+    if (
+        (index[first + np.arange(num_pages)] != 0).any()
+        or (origins != 2 * starts[first]).any()
+        or (ends < starts).any()
+        or (ends - starts > 32 * width).any()
+        or ends[-1] != words.size
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid csf_32x2_v1 exception index")
+    block = np.repeat(np.arange(r0.size), ends - starts)
+    pos = (words & 0xFF).astype(np.int64)
+    if (
+        (pos >= 64).any()
+        or (pos % 2 >= width[block]).any()
+        or ((pos[1:] <= pos[:-1]) & (block[1:] == block[:-1])).any()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("CSF exception positions must be increasing and in range")
+    out[(r0[block] + pos // 2) * cols + c0[block] + pos % 2] = words >> 8
+    return out.reshape(rows, cols)
+
+
+# weight_scale_encoding -> (stream suffixes in decoder argument order, decoder)
+CSF_SCALE_ENCODINGS: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, ...], Callable[..., np.ndarray]]] = {
+    "csf": (("nvfp4_csf_fixed", "nvfp4_csf_exceptions"), _decode_csf),
+    "csf_32x2_v1": (
+        tuple(
+            f"csf32_{name}"
+            for name in ("bases", "codes", "page_bases", "offsets", "exceptions")
+        ),
+        _decode_csf_32x2,
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def decode_csf_scale(encoding: str, streams: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rebuild one ``[rows, cols]`` float8_e4m3fn block-scale matrix."""
+    names, decode = CSF_SCALE_ENCODINGS[encoding]
+    out = decode(*(streams[name].cpu() for name in names))
+    return torch.from_numpy(out).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def csf_weights_transform(
+    encodings: Iterable[str],
+) -> Callable[[Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]], Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]]:
+    """Pair CSF scale streams back into canonical E4M3 scale tensors.
+
+    The returned transform is lazy over a ``(name, tensor)`` weight stream:
+    tensors named ``<name>.<stream>`` for a declared encoding are buffered per
+    scale and, once the encoding's stream set completes, replaced by the
+    decoded ``<name>`` tensor; everything else passes through unchanged.
+    """
+    suffixes = {
+        f".{stream}": (encoding, stream)
+        for encoding in encodings
+        for stream in CSF_SCALE_ENCODINGS[encoding][0]
+    }
+
+    def transform(
+        weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]],
+    ) -> Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
+        pending: dict[str, tuple[str, dict[str, torch.Tensor]]] = {}
+        decoded = 0
+        for name, tensor in weights:
+            for suffix, (encoding, stream) in suffixes.items():
+                if name.endswith(suffix):
+                    base = name[: -len(suffix)]
+                    break
+            else:
+                yield name, tensor
+                continue
+            if base in pending and pending[base][0] != encoding:
+                raise ValueError(f"Mixed CSF scale encodings for {base}")
+            parts = pending.setdefault(base, (encoding, {}))[1]
+            parts[stream] = tensor
+            if len(parts) == len(CSF_SCALE_ENCODINGS[encoding][0]):
+                del pending[base]
+                yield base, decode_csf_scale(encoding, parts)
+                decoded += 1
+        if pending:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"CSF scale streams without a partner: {sorted(pending)[:4]}"
+            )
+        if decoded:
+            logger.info("Decoded %d CSF scale tensors at load", decoded)
+
+    return transform

inline_comments.body: I don't think this is a correct method to deal with this. We should implement csf scale support at quantization side instead.

The checkpoint already declares `weight_scale_encoding` per layer, so ModelOpt should pick and validate it instead of the default loader guessing from tensor suffixes.

I'm considering moving the decoder under `layers/quantization/utils/` and adding a small quant-config hook in `AutoWeightsLoader` to decode the stream pairs before TP slicing. The existing checkpoint mapper only handles names, so this would be a new hook. Would that fit the direction you had in mind?

I'd keep the subdirectory shard lookup in a separate change.

I think the root cause is that we can't deal with this scale format natively and have to convert it back to E4M3 as workaround before weights loading. I don't see we have corresponding quant method implented for it, so maybe we should implement the quant method for it.
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/fa3b9d1377219247060d3c8b49eae199c9e7e154/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/modelopt.py#L2517-L2529

NVIDIA uses CSF on more than one checkpoint. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local uses `csf`, and GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local uses `csf_32x2_v1`, which lays out the streams differently. Both only put it on the routed experts.

So instead of the loader hook I mentioned above, I'd follow the `FormatScheme` pattern in `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE`. From each layer's `weight_scale_encoding`, the method would register the CSF streams as its own params and load them as they are, and `process_weights_after_loading` would decode them into `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale`. The ModelOpt config would rename the stream suffixes to match those params. The decoders would live under `layers/quantization/utils/`, keyed by encoding, so `csf_32x2_v1` gets its own params and decoder in the same place.

I haven't written this yet. So far I've loaded and served the checkpoint with this PR's decoder through a plugin, with TP=2 (nightly, MTP on) and with PP=2.

I'll add `csf_32x2_v1` in this PR as well, and split it out if you'd rather review it separately.

IIUC this accepts an encoding on any NVFP4 layer, but only `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` registers the stream params. On a linear layer the renamed `weight_scale_<stream>` names would have no param to land in, so the load either fails on an unknown name or, in a model loop that skips unknown names, leaves `weight_scale` unloaded with no error (weight tracking is off by default for quantized models). Both checkpoints only encode routed experts today, so could `get_quant_method` reject an encoding on anything that isn't `RoutedExperts`?

Done in c22209f980. `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` now registers the CSF streams named by the layer's `weight_scale_encoding` as its own params, and the ModelOpt config renames `weight_scale.<stream>` to match them. The decoders sit in `layers/quantization/utils/csf_scales.py`, keyed by encoding, with `csf_32x2_v1` next to `csf`. The default loader no longer decodes CSF.

One change from what I wrote above: the method decodes each scale matrix as soon as all of its streams have arrived, not in `process_weights_after_loading`. The streams can't be TP-sliced, so holding them until then would keep every layer's compressed scales on each rank: 4.0 GB for Qwen3.8 and 10.3 GB for GLM-5.3, summed from the checkpoint headers. The decoded matrix goes through the scale param's own weight loader, so TP and EP sharding work as they do for an uncompressed checkpoint.

A stream param fills a different param, so I mark it with `weight_loader_target`. `track_weights_loading` uses it to count the scale as loaded, and layerwise reload leaves those loaders unwrapped so the scale's wrapper buffers and counts the load. Without it, `enable_weights_track` reported the scales as missing, and reload held every CSF layer until finalize.

I also took the `tensors/` shard lookup out of this PR and will send it separately. Until then, neither checkpoint loads in full from the Hub: Qwen3.8 keeps all of its shards under `tensors/`, and GLM-5.3 keeps its attention weights there.

Checked end to end on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local with TP=2: it loads and generates correctly, and `reload_weights` processes every CSF layer and keeps the outputs unchanged. Details are in the description.

Thanks for the review, and for starting this in #60646.

1. The `tensors/` lookup is up in #64739. It also covers GLM-5.3, which keeps one shard under `tensors/` next to the root shards.
2. Agreed, only one should land. This one handles both `csf` and `csf_32x2_v1` in the quant method, so the model file doesn't need its own decoder.

Independent-implementation datapoint, in case it helps: I had a model-local CSF decoder for this exact checkpoint in #63908 (now closed as superseded by this PR). A few notes from validating it against `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local`:

- The checkpoint carries **147,456 CSF stream tensors** — all on routed experts (`mlp.experts.*` `gate/up/down_proj.weight_scale.nvfp4_csf_{fixed,exceptions}`); the `linear_attn.*` NVFP4 scales are already plain `weight_scale`. So the routed-experts-only scope here matches what the checkpoint actually needs today.
- My decoder (`base + nibble codes`, low nibble first, 24-bit position / 8-bit value exception scatter) is byte-identical in algorithm to `_decode_csf`; I diffed decoded scale bytes against the uncompressed reference on real layers and got an exact match.
- Two edge cases worth having in the tests (both covered by my 3 unit tests, happy to port): `exceptions.numel() == 0` (checkpoints with no fixups), and the `float8_e4m3fn` reinterp view must be taken on the **uint8** decoded buffer (a cast would silently reinterpret rather than re-view — the bug my PR title was about).

Also 👍 the numpy-vs-torch choice for the decode itself — at ~74K scale pairs the per-op thread-pool sync dominates; I saw that too when the torch-op version ran multi-threaded loading.

All inline threads are resolved or outdated after the move to the quantization side. @stecasta @Isotr0py could you take a fresh look at the current diff and confirm the new `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` registration addresses the placement concern from #60646? Once it's approved we can go through the `ready` label / CI path.
